name: Timely Filing PTF.1 — Provider Timely Filing Navigator
description: Walk the full Provider Timely Filing SOP: open the Timely filing pop-up and review the filing criteria and Exclusion indicator, compare State and CFT against the claim and determine the applicable filing limit, confirm the claim is Non-ITS Home, walk the corrected-claim (PX_PAJ + Frequency) and Sutter (PX_SUT) gates, verify the provider is Participating, look up the member's claim history for a prior deleted claim and confirm it was filed outside the TFL, check the PWK section for Acceptable Proof, then deny with reject code PX_R21410.

steps.name: Identify the PX_PTF hard edit on Event Resolution
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. All edits on the claim are listed; the PX_PTF edit (PX_590 — 'Claim submit time limit exceeded') is the active hard edit, flagged in red. That is the event you are resolving.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Event Resolution' tab. The active PX_PTF edit (PX_590 — 'Claim submit time limit exceeded') is shown in red as the Hard Edit you must resolve.
steps.checklistItem: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_PTF hard edit identified

steps.name: Open the Provider Information tab
steps.description: Review the timely filing limit for the claim by opening the claim and scrolling to the Provider Information tab. The timely filing reference is located in the Billing section.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Information tab.
steps.hint: Open the 'Provider Info' tab and scroll to the Billing section — the Timely Filing Limit field is here.

steps.name: Open the Timely filing pop-up
steps.description: Navigate to the Provider Information tab, then the Billing section, and click the question mark (?) icon next to the Timely Filing Limit field label. The Timely Filing pop-up window will open, with the provider's Tax ID and State fields automatically populated.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks the '?' icon, which dispatches the open_tf_popup action.
steps.hint: Click the '?' icon next to 'Timely Filing Limit' in the Billing section — the Timely filing pop-up opens with the Tax ID and State auto-populated.

steps.name: Look up TFL criteria and Exclusion indicator
steps.description: In the Timely filing pop-up, click the Search button. A row of filing criteria will appear with the fields State, CFT, Contract/LOB, Par, Effective, End date, C code, TFL, and Plan type. Note the values: State CA, CFT 52, Contract/LOB Commercial, Effective, End date, and TFL 365. Then interpret the Exclusion indicator: if Exclusion ind = No, the provider is not excluded from the 90-day rule and must submit the claim within 90 days from the date of service; if Exclusion ind = Yes, the provider is excluded and a custom timely filing limit may apply, but only if every field in the pop-up matches the corresponding value on the claim. In this scenario, the Exclusion indicator is Yes, so each field must be compared against the claim before applying the custom limit. Also compare the State displayed in the Timely Filing pop-up with the Pricing State by navigating to the Provider Information tab, then the Rendering section. Confirm that the values match. In this scenario, both fields display CA, indicating that the State requirement has been satisfied.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Search inside the Timely filing pop-up, which dispatches the tf_search action and reveals the filing-criteria rows.
steps.hint: In the Timely filing pop-up, click 'Search'. The filing-criteria rows appear — note State CA, CFT 52, Contract/LOB, Effective, End date, TFL 365, and read the Exclusion ind. Here Exclusion ind = Yes, so every field must match the claim before the custom TFL applies.
steps.checklistItem: Look up TFL criteria and Exclusion indicator

steps.name: Compare claim fields and determine the applicable filing limit
steps.description: Compare the CFT (Claim File Type) value from the Timely Filing pop-up with the claim type by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and reviewing the claim information. The CFT value must be 52 for a Professional claim and 53 for an Outpatient claim. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional; therefore, the CFT value is 52. The Contract/LOB value is treated as Commercial in this scenario and requires no further validation. Note the Receipt Date from the claim summary, along with the Billed, Allowed, Paid, and Action Code values. Compare the Receipt Date to the Effective Date and End Date displayed in the Timely Filing pop-up to determine whether it falls within the applicable date range. If Exclusion Ind = Yes and all applicable fields match the corresponding claim values, the provider must submit the claim within the timely filing limit shown in the TFL field. If Exclusion Ind = Yes but any required field does not match, the provider is subject to the 90-day filing rule. If Exclusion Ind = No, the provider is also subject to the 90-day filing rule. In this scenario, the Receipt Date does not fall within the Effective Date and End Date range shown in the Timely Filing pop-up; therefore, the provider must follow the 90-day filing rule. Also determine whether the claim is ITS Home by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and reviewing the Additional Claim Data section. If the claim type is identified as ITS Home, follow the alternate SOP steps. If the claim type is Non-ITS Home, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional, which is classified as Non-ITS Home. Therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Details sub-tab inside Claim Data to read the claim type. The Receipt-date-vs-Effective/End comparison is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Details'. Claim type is Professional → CFT 52, which matches the pop-up. The claim summary Receipt date (04/15/2026) is outside the pop-up's Effective–End range — so the 90-day rule applies.
steps.checklistItem: Compare claim fields and determine the applicable filing limit

steps.name: Check for the PX_PAJ event
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains a corrected claim event by looking for the PX_PAJ event in the Event Resolution tab. In this scenario, the PX_PAJ event is present, so the next condition (the Frequency value) must also be checked before concluding whether the claim is a corrected claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab to look for the PX_PAJ event.
steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' and look in the All Edits section — the PX_PAJ event is present. Check the Claim Header's Frequency next.

steps.name: Confirm the Frequency value
steps.description: Confirm the Frequency value by navigating to the Claim Header tab, then the General Claim Data section. A claim is considered a corrected claim when a PX_PAJ event is present and the Frequency field is set to 7. When both conditions are met, the alternate SOP for corrected claims must be followed. If either condition is not met, the claim is not considered a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step. In this scenario, the Frequency value is not 7. Therefore, the claim is not a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab to confirm the Frequency value.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' and check the Frequency field under General Claim Data. It is not 7 — so even with the PX_PAJ event this is not a corrected claim, and the trainee proceeds.

steps.name: Check for the PX_SUT event
steps.description: Determine whether the provider is Sutter by looking for the PX_SUT event in the Event Resolution tab. If the PX_SUT event is present, follow the Sutter procedure; if it is absent, the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds. In this scenario, the PX_SUT event is absent, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab again to look for the PX_SUT event.
steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' again and scan the All Edits section for a PX_SUT event — there is none, so the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds.

steps.name: Verify provider participation status
steps.description: Navigate to the Member Information tab and review the claim details. The claim type has already been confirmed as Professional. Next, navigate to the Claim Header tab, then the General Claim Data section, and review the Provider Participation field. To qualify for continued processing, the Provider Participation value must be PAR, indicating that the provider is participating. If the claim type is Professional and the provider status is PAR, proceed to the next step. If either condition is not met, follow the alternate SOP steps. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional and the provider status is PAR; therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab again to verify the Provider participation field.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' again and check the Provider Participation field under General Claim Data. It reads PAR — the claim is Professional and the provider is Participating, so proceed.

steps.name: Look up prior deleted claims
steps.description: Review the member's claim history to check whether the same claim was previously deleted due to incorrect data or because the provider data was not loaded in the database at the time. Navigate to the Search tab → Claims sub-tab — the Service from date, HCID, and Provider Tax ID are auto-populated. Enter the Service to date and click Search. Two matching claims are listed — one currently active claim with status Pending-Investigation and one with status Resolved-Cancelled. Open the Resolved-Cancelled claim's member information; if the Finalization code field shows PX_RDELEP, the claim was previously deleted.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Search on the Search → Claims sub-tab, which dispatches the claims_search action and reveals the two matching claims.
steps.hint: Open 'Search' → 'Claims', enter the Service to date, and click 'Search'. Two claims appear — open the Resolved-Cancelled claim's member information; the Finalization code PX_RDELEP confirms it was previously deleted.

steps.name: Verify the deleted claim's filing window
steps.description: To verify whether a deleted claim was filed within the timely filing limit, select View Member Information from the applicable deleted claim record, then click Open Claim Detail. Review the deleted claim details, which are displayed in the same format as the current claim. Locate the Service From Date and the Receipt Date, then calculate the difference between these dates. If the filing period falls within 90 days, the deleted claim qualifies as being filed within the TFL, and the alternate SOP steps must be followed. If there is no deleted claim, or the deleted claim falls outside the TFL, proceed with rejection. In this scenario, the deleted claim was not filed within the TFL; therefore, the trainee proceeds with rejection.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks 'Open claim detail' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, which dispatches the open_prior_claim action. The 90-day calculation is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).
steps.hint: Click 'View member information' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, then 'Open claim detail' in the dialog. Compare the claim line's Service from date with the Receipt date — the gap exceeds 90 days, so the deleted claim was outside the TFL and the trainee proceeds with rejection.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the deleted claim's filing window

steps.name: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section
steps.description: Check whether Acceptable Proof has been received to override the TFL. Navigate to the Attachments tab → Attachments sub-tab and review the PWK section. If a proof document has been submitted, the Type and Document number fields will be populated. If proof has been received and approved, apply the PX_TF bypass code and continue processing; if no proof has been received or it has not been approved, proceed to reject the claim. In this scenario, no proof has been received, so the trainee proceeds to reject the claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Attachments sub-tab on the Attachment tab to review the PWK section.
steps.hint: Open 'Attachment' → 'Attachments' and review the PWK section. The Type and Document number fields are empty — no Acceptable Proof was received, so proceed to reject the claim.
steps.checklistItem: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section

steps.name: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_R21410
steps.description: Because the provider is Participating, the claim type is Professional, and the rejection is at the claim level, apply reject code PX_R21410 as defined in the SOP. From the Action menu, select Deny Claim. A new Deny Claim section will appear below the header. Enter reject code PX_R21410 in the input box — the matching code will appear in a dropdown list — select it and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Deny Claim panel (which dispatches the deny_claim action).
steps.hint: Action menu → Deny Claim. Enter reject code PX_R21410 in the Deny Claim section, click Submit, then confirm the pop-up.
steps.checklistItem: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_R21410

steps.name: Submit Deny decision
steps.description: Navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Deny' from the dropdown menu and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the Deny decision in the submit dialog.
steps.hint: Pick 'Deny' from the Decision dropdown in the claim header, then click Submit and confirm in the dialog.

stepSummaryForResults.name: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_PTF hard edit identified
CFT matched (52), 90-day rule & Non-ITS Home confirmed
Frequency not 7 — not a corrected claim
PX_SUT event absent — provider is not Sutter
Deleted claim confirmed outside the TFL
No Acceptable Proof in PWK section
Deny Claim panel submitted with PX_R21410
